compare.title: Notalo vs. MusicXML-Based Tools — Two Ways to Add Note Names
compare.intro: Most note-naming tools require a MusicXML file to start. Notalo works directly from a photo or PDF. Here's how the two approaches compare.
compare.other_prep: Export to MusicXML first, using notation software
compare.notalo_free: Unlimited — completely free, supported by ads
compare.notalo_save: Not applicable — files deleted after processing
compare.other_save: Some tools offer score libraries and sharing
compare.notalo_best: Sheet music you only have as a photo, scan, or print
compare.conclusion: If your sheet music exists only as a photo, a PDF, or a printed page, Notalo skips the file-conversion step entirely. If you already work in MusicXML and want a score library with sharing, a MusicXML-based tool may fit better.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: PDF, JPG, and PNG — sheet music files up to 20MB.
faq.q2: Do I need MusicXML or notation software?
faq.a2: No. Just upload a photo or PDF of your sheet music as-is — Notalo detects noteheads directly from the image.
faq.a3: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up, credits, or payment required. The site is supported by ads.
faq.a4: English (C D E), Italian (Do Re Mi), Japanese (ドレミ), and German (C D E H).
faq.a5: No. Uploaded files and results are deleted immediately after processing.
faq.a6: Clean, printed sheet music: a PDF exported from notation software or a sharp, straight scan. The model was trained on printed notation, so smudged copies, faded prints, hand-drawn scans and photos taken at an angle can miss or mislabel notes. If you have the original PDF, upload that.

processing.title: Converting your sheet music…
processing.sub: Usually 5–20 seconds per page. Keep this tab open.
processing.tip.1: Middle C sits on the first ledger line below the treble staff — and on the first ledger line above the bass staff.
processing.tip.2: A sharp or flat in the key signature applies to every octave, all the way through the piece.
processing.tip.3: Practice slowly: play a passage correctly three times in a row before speeding up.
processing.tip.4: A dot after a note adds half its value — a dotted half note lasts three beats.
processing.tip.5: Treble clef lines from the bottom: E G B D F. Spaces: F A C E.
processing.tip.6: Bass clef lines from the bottom: G B D F A. Spaces: A C E G.
